tools.name: search_lessons
tools.description: Find AI PM Lab lessons on a topic (e.g. RAG, evals, agents, prompt injection, cost). Returns the best matches with their key idea and link.

tools.name: get_lesson
tools.description: A lesson's key idea, concepts, things to try and suggested prompts, with links to the lesson, its 3D tour and its challenge.

tools.name: list_challenges
tools.description: The challenges (games scored from real recorded runs, with leaderboards) and what each asks you to do.

tools.name: define
tools.description: A plain-language definition of an AI product concept (tokens, temperature, RAG, embeddings, LLM-as-judge, prompt injection…), with the lessons that teach it.

tools.name: count_tokens
tools.description: Count the tokens in a text (an estimate with OpenAI's cl100k tokenizer; other model families differ slightly).

tools.name: estimate_cost
tools.description: What a model call costs per request, per day and per month at a given volume, from AI Gateway's live prices. Model ids look like 'openai/gpt-4.1-mini' or 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5'.

tools.name: compare_models
tools.description: Compare several models side by side at a given volume: cost per request and per month, prices, context window, output limit, release date and knowledge cutoff, from AI Gateway's live catalog. Pass ids like 'openai/gpt-4.1-mini', or a provider name ('anthropic', 'openai', 'google') for its newest mod

tools.name: list_experiments
tools.description: The real runs recorded on one of AI PM Lab's 3D pages or lessons, each described by its setup (e.g. which defences or settings were on). Replay one to see what happened.

tools.name: replay_experiment
tools.description: What happened in one recorded real run (e.g. whether a prompt injection leaked data with given defences, or how many answers were made up without a facts sheet): the setup, each step, the result and the model's reply, with a link to run it on the site.

tools.name: quiz_me
tools.description: A round from AI PM Lab's challenges, built from real recorded runs: Call It (predict what a model did), Spot the Failure (ship or flag a real output) or Which Wins? (pick the better of two setups). Returns the question without its answer; call again with the round id and the user's choice to mark it

tools.name: review_ai_spec
tools.description: Check an AI feature spec or PRD against what AI PM Lab teaches: approach, model and cost, prompt, grounding, output contract, tools, security, human oversight, evals, monitoring, fallbacks. Gaps link to lessons. Returns instructions to follow with the user's text.

tools.name: prep_planning_meeting
tools.description: The questions a PM should ask engineers about a planned AI feature, with why each matters and what a good answer sounds like. Returns instructions to follow with the user's text.

tools.name: design_eval_suite
tools.description: Build an evaluation suite for a planned AI feature with AI PM Lab's method: test cases (typical, edge, out of scope, attacks), graders with a judge rubric, pass bars, and a JSON test set. Returns instructions to follow with the user's text.

tools.name: write_acceptance_criteria
tools.description: Acceptance criteria for an AI feature or user story that can actually be tested: Given/When/Then with measurable pass bars on a test set, must-pass safety criteria, latency and cost budgets, and example test cases, ready to paste into a ticket. Returns instructions to follow with the user's text.

tools.name: price_ai_feature
tools.description: Work out an AI feature's unit economics and pricing: cost per request and per user (light, typical, heavy), levers like caching and routing, pricing options with margins, guardrails, and the assumptions to validate. Returns instructions to follow with the user's text.

tools.name: launch_readiness_review
tools.description: A go/no-go review of an AI feature's launch plan: evals, grounding, attacks, approvals, cost, latency, monitoring, rollout and support, each marked ready, at risk or missing, with blockers and a launch-day watch list. Returns instructions to follow with the user's text.

tools.name: ai_incident_review
tools.description: A blameless post-incident review for an AI feature: where it failed (input, retrieval, prompt, model, tools, output checks), why evals and monitoring missed it, actions, and the new eval cases that would catch it next time. Returns instructions to follow with the user's text.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: review_ai_spec, launch_readiness_review · Private data: define, count_tokens · Public sink: ai_incident_review · Destructive: replay_experiment, design_eval_suite, ai_incident_review.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: review_ai_spec, launch_readiness_review · Private data: define, count_tokens · Public sink: ai_incident_review · Destructive: replay_experiment, design_eval_suite, ai_incident_review

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_experiments" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "The real runs recorded on one of AI PM Lab's 3D pages, each described by its setup. Replay one to see what happened." → after: "The real runs recorded on one of AI PM Lab's 3D pages or lessons, each described by its setup (e.g. which defences or settings were on). Replay one to see what happened."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
